reason: Refuted on the source line only; the citation is otherwise the strongest of the four. I opened what the verifier did not: the Internet Archive scan of Letters of Rainer Maria Rilke 1892-1910, Norton 1945 (lettersofrainerm030932mbp), full-text OCR and page-level OCR. The letter is headed To Clara Rilke, Villa Discopoli, Capri (Italy), January 1, 1907, and the sentence reads word for word as proposed, including tasks, claims, and demands and bestow upon those who demand of it necessary, serious, and great things. The page-level OCR puts the printed folio 253 at the head of the page that carries the sentence and 254 at the head of the next, so p. 253 is right (Google Books PA253 agrees). Translator and year right. shipped.js clean, Rilke count 0, not banned; Correspondence is the form. The fault: the source line carries a dash, the en dash in 1892–1910. Rule 5 bans the em dash and the check here says carry no dash; the verifier's own other sources write 1881 to 1882 and 1891 to 1892, so house style is the word to. Ship it with the corrected source above (129 characters). Note is empty, so nothing else to fix. On fame (rule 2) the passage is a standing New Year quotation (WIST lists it among its most-visited entries, usually in paraphrase), which is a fame signal, not proof; the editor may want the note to say the line is printed from the Norton translation, not the circulating paraphrase.
